commitResults.messageBody: Move command input, the startup banner, separators, task rendering, confirmations, and error messages out of Duck. Keep command orchestration and storage behavior unchanged so later Parser, Storage, and TaskList extractions can proceed independently.

Give Storage ownership of the configurable data path, atomic saves, startup loading, record decoding, and saved-date validation. Make Duck delegate persistence while retaining rollback coordination, isolating filesystem concerns without changing console behavior.

Replace Duck's raw ArrayList with TaskList operations for lookup, addition, positional restoration, deletion, marking, and unmarking. Pass immutable task snapshots to Ui and Storage while preserving save-failure rollback behavior and task ordering.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract user command parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce CommandType to model supported command syntax and move command recognition, task-number conversion, task construction, event field parsing, and deadline validation out of Duck. Keep list-dependent range checks and command execution in Duck, and add a UI regression case for exact command boundaries and prefix collisions.

Define the shared execute and exit-state contract for command objects, then move farewell behavior into the first concrete command. Keep all other dispatch paths unchanged so this initial stretch-goal increment remains small and independently verifiable.

Move list display behavior behind the Command execution contract so Duck no longer formats or exposes the task collection for the list command. Keep parsing and the remaining command paths unchanged to make this a small, independently tested refactoring step.

Encapsulate the parsed task together with its add, persist, rollback, and confirmation behavior. Reuse the same command for todo, deadline, and event inputs while leaving syntax validation in Parser, reducing Duck's responsibilities without changing user-visible behavior.

Encapsulate the selected task number together with list-range validation, deletion, persistence rollback, and confirmation output. Restore a task at its original index when saving fails, and leave numeric syntax parsing in Parser so each class retains one clear responsibility.

Introduce a shared TaskStatusCommand template for task-number validation, status mutation, persistence, and rollback. Add focused MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand subclasses for their target states and confirmation messages, removing Duck's final command-execution helpers without duplicating transaction logic.

Move concrete command selection and argument binding into Parser.parse, keeping recognition and argument helpers private. Replace Duck's command-specific switch with uniform parse, execute, and exit-check logic so new commands can be added without expanding the application loop.

Make Duck own Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList state; load tasks during construction while deferring any error display until after the greeting; and move the command loop into run. Reduce main to constructing and starting the application, and centralize response separators in the run loop so normal, error, and exit paths remain consistent.
Group commands, tasks, parsing, storage, and UI classes into focused packages while keeping src/main/java as the source root. Update the application and UI test entry points for duck.Duck.
Merge the provided Gradle configuration and configure it to launch duck.Duck using Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for core application logic
commitResults.messageBody: Cover task-list operations, command parsing, persistence, and mutating command rollback behavior. Document the 50% high-value method coverage target.
Set the Shadow JAR output name to Duck.jar for standalone distribution.

Java sources contain inconsistent naming, indentation, and JavaDoc
parameter descriptions, which makes the codebase harder to read and
maintain.

Apply the SE-EDU coding standard across production classes. Clarify task
and event names, align switch cases, and normalize documentation while
preserving application behavior.

Future Java changes need a consistent, reusable interpretation of the
SE-EDU coding standard.

Add project guidance and a mechanical style checker, and require agents
to apply both before verifying Java changes.

Future commits need consistent messages and branch names that follow the
SE-EDU Git conventions.

Add reusable project guidance and a mechanical commit-message checker,
and require agents to apply them before every commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command with input validation
commitResults.messageBody:
Users need a way to locate tasks without inspecting the entire task list.

Add case-insensitive keyword searching and reject empty keywords. Display matching tasks without changing saved data, and cover valid searches and error cases with JUnit and UI regression tests.

Duck is limited to a console interface.

Users need a more approachable way to manage tasks with clear visual
separation between their commands and Duck's responses.

Add a responsive graphical chat interface that reuses the existing
command, task, storage, and error-handling behavior. Separate visual
layout and styling from interaction logic so the interface remains easy
to maintain.

Preserve the console workflow, show startup and farewell messages, and
close the window three seconds after a valid bye command. Add focused
tests for the new response boundary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Checkstyle and fix test formatting
commitResults.messageBody:
Automate SE-EDU Java style checks with the official configuration.

Reformat assertion lambdas without changing test behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use varargs for multi-line UI output
commitResults.messageBody:
UI response methods repeat individual println calls when emitting
multiple lines, making related output harder to read as one unit.

Introduce a varargs helper for ordered lines and reuse it across
multi-line responses while preserving the existing console output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Assert command before extracting arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
The extractArguments method assumes that parseCommand has already
recognized the command type. Assert that the input begins with the
expected command word.

setTaskStatus is expected to apply the requested completion state.
Assert that the task's resulting state matches the requested state to
detect internal programming errors.

TaskList.add is expected to append exactly one task. Assert that the
task count increases and that the new task occupies the final position.

Stored statuses are validated before task reconstruction. Assert that
the reconstructed task matches its saved completion state to detect
internal loading errors.

parseTask combines common validation, type dispatch, type-specific
field checks, object construction, and status restoration in one
conditional chain. This obscures the persistence flow and makes future
task-type changes riskier.

Decompose the decoder into focused helpers so the main method reads at
one level of abstraction. Preserve validation order, persisted formats,
and user-facing errors to keep the refactoring behavior-neutral.

Task filtering and storage-string conversion use temporary mutable
lists and explicit loops despite being direct collection operations.

Use stream filter and map pipelines to express their intent directly.
Retain encounter order and unmodifiable results while reducing mutable
intermediate state.
Clarify command documentation and rename the deadline date field to better communicate its purpose.

commitResults.messageTitle: Event: Replace positional times with named fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Event stores its start and end values in a two-element array. Readers
must remember each index's meaning, and invalid index use can compile
without exposing the mistake.

Replace the positional representation with startTime and endTime
fields. Preserve the existing display and persistence formats while
making each value's purpose explicit.

Event exposes a constructor that accepts an unvalidated combined time
range, but no production or test code calls it. Keeping the overload
adds an unsupported path that can fail through array indexing.

Remove the dead constructor so every event is created with explicit
start and end values. This narrows the API and prevents unused parsing
logic from obscuring the supported construction path.

TaskList preallocates space for 100 tasks without evidence that this capacity is needed. The unexplained value acts as a magic number and introduces a premature optimization.\n\nUse the default ArrayList capacity so the collection grows according to actual usage. Preserve all task-list behavior while removing the unnecessary assumption.

MainWindow repeats the three-second exit delay in transition setup, user-facing text, and documentation. These copies can become inconsistent when the delay changes.\n\nStore the delay once in seconds and derive both the transition and message from it. Keep the existing timing and visible behavior.

Parser and Storage independently enforce identical deadline date shape, calendar, and year rules. Keeping two copies risks inconsistent validation between command input and saved records.\n\nMove canonical validation to DeadlineDateParser and let each caller translate failures into its existing contextual error message. Add focused tests for valid boundaries and invalid dates.
Refactor collection transformations with streams
Remove an invalid return and compare the reconstructed task against its saved status so storage loading compiles and validates the correct value.

Deadline commands require canonical ISO dates, which makes common
near-term dates cumbersome to enter.

Accept case-insensitive weekday abbreviations and resolve them to the
strictly next occurrence while keeping saved dates canonical. Document
the syntax and cover supported and rejected inputs.
Deadline: Support weekday abbreviations

commitResults.messageTitle: GUI: Distinguish user and Duck messages
commitResults.messageBody:
The conversation participants have fixed roles, but their message
presentation does not identify them explicitly.

Add compact speaker labels and use asymmetric alignment and colours so
users can scan the conversation and identify each speaker quickly.

Invalid-command responses share the same visual treatment as successful
Duck replies, which makes failures easy to overlook.

Track whether the latest GUI response represents an error and render it
with a warning label, pale-red background, and contrasting border. Add
tests to ensure the error state follows the latest command.

Message bubbles use a fixed narrow width even when the application
window has more space, while very wide lines reduce readability.

Scale each bubble with the available dialog width and retain an upper
limit. Preserve wrapping so the conversation adapts cleanly as the
window is resized.

commitResults.messageTitle: GUI: Let welcome message wrap naturally
commitResults.messageBody:
The graphical greeting contains a forced line break, so it stays on two
lines even when the window has enough space.

Replace the console-oriented line break with a space at the GUI boundary
and update the response test. Preserve the console greeting format.

commitResults.messageTitle: GUI: Refine chat spacing and typography
commitResults.messageBody:
The interface uses separate font settings and generous gaps that make
the conversation less compact than needed.

Adopt the system font, standardize control and bubble padding, and
reduce vertical spacing between messages. Keep bold weight for speaker
and error labels to preserve hierarchy.

Large avatars compete with message content and consume valuable space in
the compact chat window.

Reduce both participant images to a smaller consistent size and soften
their shadows. Keep the existing transparent artwork and speaker labels
so each participant remains easy to identify.

New users see a greeting and empty input field without examples of valid
commands or a hint about where to begin.

Add concise examples to the graphical welcome message and descriptive
placeholder text to the command field. Keep the existing Enter shortcut
and automatic scrolling behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: Give Duck a friendly personality
commitResults.messageBody:
Duck's responses are functional but do not express a consistent
character or guide users after an unknown command.

Give greetings, confirmations, errors, and empty states a restrained
duck theme. Add a help command so recovery guidance points to a real
feature, and test the new user-facing responses.

The chat relies on a recognizable third-party character and has few
visual cues connecting normal replies to Duck's personality.

Use an original transparent mascot and a restrained yellow accent.
Prefix successful state changes with a checkmark while retaining the
deadline tag and error warning for quick scanning.

The user guide does not explain Duck's character, visual language, or
complete command set.

Replace the placeholders with a concise product introduction, visual
cue legend, command summary, and examples for each task type.

Repeated mark or unmark commands rewrite storage even when a task is
already in the requested state.

Reject no-op status changes before mutation or persistence and explain
the existing status. Test both completed and active task paths.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Add recovery guidance to errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Several command errors identify the problem but leave users to infer
the valid syntax or available task numbers.

Append concise examples to todo and deadline errors, and direct invalid
task-number commands to list the available tasks. Align missing and
malformed task numbers under the same actionable response.

Blank or whitespace-only input creates an error bubble even though the
user has not submitted a command.

Ignore blank submissions before parsing, clear stray whitespace, and
return focus to the input field for the next command.

commitResults.messageTitle: GUI: Recover from unexpected command failures
commitResults.messageBody:
An unexpected runtime failure can escape the JavaFX event handler and
leave the chat without a useful response.

Catch failures at the GUI boundary, retain diagnostic details in the
error log, and show a safe error bubble while keeping input usable.

Repeated add commands create indistinguishable task records and make
task numbers harder to manage.

Compare task type, description, and date or time details before
mutating or saving the list. Report the existing task number and
preserve distinct tasks that share only some fields.

Event times are otherwise free-form, so comparing every value could
reject valid descriptive text.

When both endpoints use yyyy-MM-dd HHmm, parse them strictly. Reject
invalid date-times or an end before the start, while keeping free-form
values compatible. Document and test the rule.

The command metadata flag uses a predicate name that can be mistaken
for a non-boolean value during standards checks.

Rename the field, parameter, and accessor to canAcceptArguments so their
boolean meaning is explicit without changing command parsing behavior.

Test results alone do not show which production paths remain untested.

Generate HTML and XML coverage reports after each test run using a
Java 25-compatible JaCoCo version. Document the report location so
coverage gaps can guide later test additions.

Duck's response boundary has limited coverage for loading failures and
multi-command persistence behavior.

Add integration tests for saved-task loading, malformed data, duplicate
rejection, state changes across a restart, and response flag resets.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test: Expand console UI message coverage
commitResults.messageBody:
Several user-facing messages are covered only through broader command
tests, making formatting regressions harder to locate.

Add focused checks for numbered lists, status messages, help and error
output, and singular or plural task counts at key boundaries.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test: Cover task display and identity
commitResults.messageBody:
Task formatting and equality-like identity checks are mostly exercised
indirectly through storage and list tests.

Add focused tests for every task type covering status display, escaped
storage records, matching details, and meaningful differences.

Structured event validation has edge cases at equal times, date changes,
calendar limits, and the free-form compatibility boundary.

Add parser tests for equal and later endpoints, leap-day rollover,
supported year limits, and mixed structured and free-form values.

Coverage reports provide visibility but do not prevent later
regressions.

Require 90% line and 80% branch coverage for automatically testable
classes during check. Keep JavaFX window and launcher classes under the
documented manual-testing workflow.
